summary: A 1930s L-4 lookout near Seeley Lake, staffed into the 1980s, now an NRHP-listed Recreation.gov rental overlooking the Swan Mountains.

facts.design: L-4 cab with catwalk atop a 20-foot slanting pole tower; 14x14 ft cabin

access.note: Open to the public as a Recreation.gov rental; access road is steep dirt/gravel, high-clearance vehicle recommended

visit.trail_note: Reached by vehicle via a steep dirt and gravel access road; no hiking trail noted

facts.agency: U.S. Forest Service, Lolo National Forest

events.note: National Historic Lookout Register gives 1932 as the build year
Recreation.gov and firelookout.com both give 1933 instead; sources disagree by one year
Recreation.gov says staffed by Forest Service employees until the mid-1980s, when it opened for recreation
NHLR instead says the tower has been used only on an emergency basis since 1989
Added to the National Historic Lookout Register February 26, 1996

resolved_conflicts.explanation: NHLR states 1932; Recreation.gov and firelookout.com both state 1933. The story reports both figures rather than picking one, since neither source gives a reason to prefer it over the other.

Recreation.gov says staffed until the mid-1980s; NHLR says used only on an emergency basis since 1989. These are not necessarily contradictory (a transition period between regular and emergency-only use is plausible) but the story notes both rather than merging them into one date.

sources.title: Double Arrow Lookout, Lolo National Forest

evidence.supports: built 1932, before a road reached site, L-4 cab on 20' slanting pole tower, used only on emergency basis since 1989, popular viewpoint
evidence.quote: Double Arrow lookout was built in 1932 before a road led to the site. It is an L-4 cab with catwalk atop a 20' slanting pole tower. Used only on an emergency basis since 1989, it is popular with valley residents as a viewpoint.

evidence.supports: built 1933, staffed until mid-80s, 14x14 structure on 20ft tower, facilities, access road high-clearance
evidence.quote: It was built in 1933 and staffed by Forest Service employees until the mid-'80s, when it was opened to the public for recreation purposes.

evidence.supports: NRHP listing 100002041 and NHLR registration date
evidence.quote: Description Located on a low hill near Seeley Lake, Montana

evidence.supports: built 1933, L-4 cab on 20' pole tower, staffed into mid-1980s
evidence.quote: This 20' pole tower with L-4 cab, built in 1933, was staffed into the mid-1980's.

evidence.supports: cabin facilities: electric lights, heat, cook stove, refrigerator, two platforms, two cots, vault toilet
evidence.quote: The facility has electric lights, heat, a cook stove and a small refrigerator.

evidence.supports: access road steep dirt/gravel, high-clearance recommended; view of Seeley valley and Swan Mountains
evidence.quote: The lookout can be accessed by vehicle, however, the steep dirt and gravel road requires high-clearance vehicles.

notes_for_editor: Brief's existing record (built 1933, L-4, 6.1m height) is consistent with Recreation.gov/firelookout.com; only NHLR's page gives 1932 instead, so the story reports the one-year discrepancy rather than silently picking a side. NRHP reference number 100002041 taken from the brief's register field, which matches NHLR's own cross-reference. No newspaper coverage or NRHP nomination PDF was consulted; confidence is high because three independent, consistent descriptive sources exist even though they disagree on the exact year.
